newsitem.title: USA: Chicago woman lives without heartbeat for hours.
newsitem.headline: Chicago woman lives without heartbeat for hours.

text.p: A woman whose heart stopped beating for hours when she spent the night in a car during severe cold was released from a hospital Monday after recovering, doctors said.
The 67-year-old woman told reporters she did not remember how or why she wound up in the car on the night of Jan. 18 when temperatures fell below zero Fahrenheit (-17.7 Celsius).

Doctors at Loyola University Medical Centre said the woman's heart had not beaten for hours and her body temperature had fallen to about 75 degrees Fahrenheit (23.8 Celsius) -- more than 20 degrees below normal -- when she was brought into the hospital Jan. 19.
The woman was placed on a heart-lung machine and her body temperature returned to normal in about two hours at which time her heart was shocked to restart it.
Doctors said she survived without a heartbeat because the cold slowed her metabolism, limiting her body's need for oxygen.
The woman, who lives in North Riverside, near Chicago, suffered a limited amount of frostbite on her fingertips and kneecaps but otherwise was walking and conversing normally, the hospital said.
